answers.question:
Question 9: Here is the smallest tool set I propose, with what each call can answer. Please confirm it.
- list the customer's orders: answers with each of the signed-in customer's orders, cancelled ones included, each with its refund or none; or gets no answer.
- cancel an order (order number): answers "cancelled"; answers that the order has shipped since it was read; or gets no answer.
- issue the refund for an order (order number): answers with the refund, pending or issued; with a refund whose status is failed (a final error); with a temporary error and no refund; with "order not cancelled"; or times out.
- ask staff to follow up (order number, reason): answers that the task is created, or gets no answer.
Claims put to the owner: C-06, C-09, C-11.
answers.recommended: Yes, that is the tool set, and those are the answers each call can give.
answers.reply:
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.
> Confirmed, with four changes:
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> 2. issue_refund adds outcome OrderNotCancelled.
> 3. request_staff_followup is idempotent on (order_number, reason) — add as SG-03. On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.
> 4. list_orders includes cancelled orders. Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: Question 10: Your order system has no docs, so I compared it with common order systems. In those, sending the same refund call twice can make two refunds unless the system checks for one that already exists. (Your payment provider's docs say a repeated request is safe only when it carries the same idempotency key.) Here is where it matters, in plain steps: the customer has one open order and asks to cancel it; the agent proposes, the customer says yes; the cancel works; the refund call times out, though the refund was made; the agent sends the refund call once more, as you said; it answers with a refund; the order now has two refunds, against your rule of at most one refund per order. If a second refund call for an order that already has a refund just returns that refund, the agent can resend as you said. If it makes a second refund, the agent should re-read first. Does a second refund call for an order that already has a refund make a second refund? Claims put to the owner: C-16.
answers.recommended: Treat it as possible. After a refund call that times out, the agent re-reads the order's refund before sending the call again, and sends it again only when the re-read shows no refund.
answers.reply: > Tool contract: issue_refund(order_number) is idempotent, keyed on order number — repeated calls return the same refund id and never create a second refund. The store enforces this (supporting-actor guarantee, Appendix B). The agent may retry it.

answers.question: Question 11: When the cancel call gets no answer, the order may or may not have been cancelled. What should the agent do? Claims put to the owner: C-10.
answers.recommended: The agent re-reads the order. If it shows the order cancelled, the agent issues the refund. If it shows the order not cancelled, the agent tells the customer the order was not cancelled and nothing was changed. If the re-read gets no answer, the agent says the outcome is unknown, issues no refund, and asks staff to follow up (cancellation unknown).
answers.reply: > If the cancel call times out: no blind resend; re-read the order. Cancelled, continue to refund. Still placed or processing, send the cancel once more under the same confirmation. Shipped, report it and issue no refund. Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.

answers.question: Question 12: The refund call returns the amount it refunded. What does the agent do when that amount differs from the total paid the customer said yes to? Claims put to the owner: C-29.
answers.recommended: The agent makes no further change with the new amount, tells the customer the amount the refund call returned, and asks staff to follow up with a new reason, "refund amount differs".
